analysis.title: GS Housing Market Activity Scale: Week of October 25: Weekly Scale Flat Sequentially While September Monthly Reading Declines 4%
key_insights: The GS weekly housing activity scale for the week of October 25 was flat sequentially and down 11% YoY, 33% below the long-term average. Better mortgage applications and median listing price were offset by weaker sales, days on market and homes off market in two weeks.
The 30-year mortgage rate fell 8bps to 7.24% for the week of October 25 (Freddie Mac), but is up 107bps YoY.
The GS monthly scale fell 4% sequentially in September and was down 9% YoY, 23% below the long-term average. New construction and resale components were -4% and -3%, versus -1% and -4% in August.

New construction is 25% below its long-term average and resale is 10% below. The new construction decline was led by weaker homebuilder sentiment, completions, starts, price and permits. Units under construction and new home sales were flat.
Existing home sales fell 1% in September and price fell 36bps, while the 30-year mortgage rate rose to 6.86% for the month.
Builder results, commentary and GS channel checks point to a meaningful slowdown in September, with October flat sequentially. GS expects this to hold into early November at least.
Conditions could improve after the elections and if the Middle East conflict is resolved, which could push rates and inflation lower.

GS is focused on names with company-specific initiatives, including potential capital allocation, and highlights Buy-rated IBP. If conditions improve, GS sees the most upside in MTH and DHI because of their entry-level exposure and disciplined balance of margins and cash use.

Weekly strengths: median sale price flat YoY, sale-to-list ratio 98.3% (43bps above the same week of 2019), time on market 2 days below 2019, 27% of homes off market within 2 weeks versus 26% in 2019, active listings up 2% YoY and 2% below 2019.
Weekly weaknesses: home sales down 6% YoY and 3% sequentially, median list price down 1% YoY, purchase applications down 18% YoY but up 4% sequentially and 13% below the September average.
Total mortgage applications fell 42% YoY and refinancings fell 61% YoY. ARMs were 11% of volume, up 80bps sequentially, versus 9% a year ago.
Purchase applications are 1% above the February 2025 trough as rates move off their recent 52-week high. GS expects continued volatility.

Three-month data to September: existing for-sale supply is 15% below September 2019, with single-family prices up 2% YoY. Existing single-family sales fell 1% YoY and are 24% below the 2015-19 average. New single-family sales are 13% above the 2015-19 average but down 3% YoY. Single-family starts of 878,000 fell 1% YoY. New home prices fell 4% YoY and are 11% off the October 2022 peak.
The September NAHB Housing Market Index fell 1pt sequentially but is up 4% YoY at 34.

Since 2010 the monthly scale has a 63% correlation to a cap-weighted index of six homebuilder stocks (DHI, KBH, LEN, MTH, PHM, TOL). It has a 39% correlation to trailing 4-quarter orders, which GS forecasts will fall 2% YoY in 4Q26 for covered builders.

tension_points.bull_case: Weekly data show sale-to-list at 98.3%, time on market below 2019, active listings 2% below 2019 and resale inventory 15% below 2019. Builders are using incentives to support sales, and the GS scale correlates 63% with homebuilder stocks. GS sees greater activity if headwinds abate.
tension_points.bear_case: The weekly scale is 33% below its long-term average and down 11% YoY. Mortgage rates are 7.24%, home sales are down 6% YoY, and purchase applications are down 18% YoY. Builder results and channel checks show a meaningful September slowdown.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Conditions staying flat into early November, with no improvement after the elections or a Middle East resolution that lowers rates and inflation.
